response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT o.ordertune, COUNT(DISTINCT o.recordvault) AS cnt FROM orders o JOIN riskandmargin r ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.ordertune), a AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM c) SELECT AVG(c.cnt) AS avg_count, AVG(c.cnt - a.avg_cnt) AS avg_excess FROM c CROSS JOIN a WHERE c.cnt > a.avg_cnt

assumptions.assumption: Orders are identified by recordvault (the unique order reference), so distinct orders are counted on recordvault.
The average across types is taken over only the order types that have at least one matched order. Types with zero matches do not appear in the grouping.
If no type is above average (for example, all counts are equal), the query returns one row with NULLs.
